messages.content: Let's finish San Diego. Please confirm the split-stay totals and the cancellation rules one more time, then reserve both rooms. I also want the car only while we're at the coast if that still makes financial sense.

The four Bahia nights, June 9-13, total $1,903.44 including taxes and mandatory charges. The two InterContinental nights, June 13-15, total $975.18, also including taxes and mandatory charges. Lodging is $2,878.62 altogether. The current transportation estimate for returning the car downtown Friday is $533.40: $318.40 for the rental, $55 for fuel, and $160 for rides after the return.
And how does that compare with keeping the rental through Sunday?

Keeping it through Sunday would be about $628.60 once the two additional rental days, waterfront parking, and extra fuel are included. Returning it Friday saves an estimated $95.20 and avoids having a parked car during the waterfront portion.
Good. What exactly are the hotel deposit and cancellation deadlines? I don't want a vague summary before you charge anything.

For the Bahia, a $475.86 one-night deposit is charged at booking. Cancellation is free through 4:00 p.m. Pacific time on June 6; after that, the deposit is forfeited. The remaining $1,427.58 is due at the hotel. For the InterContinental, the card guarantees the reservation but is not charged now. That rate may be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. Pacific time on June 1. Beginning June 2, the full $975.18 becomes nonrefundable and will be charged if canceled or if you do not arrive.
So the waterfront room has the earlier and much larger cancellation exposure, even though there is no deposit today.
Correct. The Bahia's late-cancellation risk is one night, $475.86, starting June 6. The InterContinental's risk is the entire two-night amount, $975.18, starting June 2.
All right. Reserve one two-queen room at each hotel for the three of us. Use the dates you just gave and the card already on file.

Both rooms are reserved. The Bahia two-queen room is confirmed for June 9-13 under BA-SD-61842; $475.86 was charged today, with $1,427.58 due at the property. The InterContinental two-queen room is confirmed for June 13-15 under IC-SD-90417; no charge was made today, and the guaranteed total is $975.18.
Now set up the car. We land at 10:17 Monday. I want enough time to collect the checked bag, and on Friday we should drop our luggage at the waterfront hotel before returning the car.

A sensible schedule is pickup at the SAN rental center at 11:15 a.m. Monday, June 9, and return at the downtown branch at 10:00 a.m. Friday, June 13. On Friday, drive to the InterContinental first, leave the bags with the bell desk, then take the car to the downtown return location. The branch is close enough that the three of you can walk back or take a short ride if needed.
Does the $318.40 include the downtown return fee, taxes, and an additional driver for my spouse?

Yes. The $318.40 total includes taxes, the downtown drop fee, and one additional authorized driver. Fuel is not included. It is a pay-at-pickup reservation with free cancellation until the scheduled pickup time.
Book that midsize car, then give me the final trip total and tell me what is still only an estimate.

The midsize car is reserved under SD-RC-33759 for pickup at 11:15 a.m. June 9 and downtown return at 10:00 a.m. June 13. The confirmed rental price is $318.40, payable at pickup. The complete working trip total remains $6,015.62: $1,454 for flights and the expected checked bag, $2,878.62 for hotels, $533.40 for transportation, $204.60 for zoo admission, and $945 for meals. Within that total, the hotel and rental base amounts are confirmed; the $80 checked-bag charge, $55 fuel, $160 in rides, zoo admission, and meal spending remain estimates or unpurchased items. The Friday bag-drop and downtown car-return plan is now settled. Zoo timing and any separate waterfront dinner or additional paid activity allowance are still open.
